source_updates.title: A DDSP Framework for Adaptive Room Equalization
findings: paper Table 1 and bundled repository results use different transition times and algorithm sets
paper midpoint and zero-gain initialization is replaced by random initialization of all 21 normalized EQ parameters in public code
the first public-code gradient path starts from the target response rather than the initial RIR when use_true_LEM is false
target minimum-phase conversion includes an undocumented division by two and evaluation adds a fixed 300-sample reference delay
negative SI-SDR does not establish minimal change or phase preservation
the informal listening statement lacks a reproducible protocol
source_updates.limited_conclusion: The paper supports calibration research, but public defaults and bundled results are not a parity reproduction and require clean manifested raw-output evaluation.

source_updates.title: A Clipping Prevention Method for All-Pass Digital Filters with Time-Varying Coefficients
findings: the Direct Form I discrete-sample bound does not prove reconstructed true-peak or other-topology internal-state safety
the second-order equal headroom split is sufficient but not demonstrated optimal
the guard changes the coefficient and phase trajectory beyond the dangerous instant
reported runtime is batch throughput rather than worst-case callback latency
one music example without controlled listening cannot establish transparency
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Treat the method as a topology-specific sample-safety candidate requiring independent state, true-peak, phase and listening tests.

source_updates.title: Clipping prevention in time-varying parametric equalizers based on first-order allpass filters
findings: same first author supervisors and first-order all-pass method as the DAFx paper
PDF is unavailable and all rights reserved
lineage evidence rather than independent replication
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Record as same-family metadata only and do not infer inaccessible content.

knowledge_cards.claim: Independent peak normalization destroys gain-dependent evidence but not scale-invariant SI-SDR by scaling alone.
Raw gain-preserving outputs and loudness-matched listening copies serve different evaluation purposes.
Reused result directories plus wildcard aggregation can contaminate experiment cardinality and rankings.
A bundled result subset with different conditions is not a reproduction of a paper main table.
Random filter initialization is not equivalent to midpoint parameters with zero gains.
A target-response gradient-path initialization is not perfect initial-RIR knowledge.
An undocumented target factor of one half is a controller-level gain choice rather than neutral serialization.
A fixed reference delay needs derivation or an alignment sensitivity sweep for every RIR.
Negative SI-SDR cannot by itself prove minimal change or phase preservation.
An informal listening statement without protocol is not perceptual evidence.
A Direct Form I discrete-sample bound does not generalize to reconstructed true peak or arbitrary internal states.
A same-author predecessor abstract establishes lineage rather than independent replication.
